root_added_source_correction_complete.entire_available_original_abstract:
Background

Leucine, a branched-chain amino acid (BCAA), is an effective nutritional strategy to enhance skeletal muscle mass in aging populations. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of oral leucine-enriched BCAA supplementation on muscle mass, muscle synthesis biomarkers, and physical performance in elderly patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD).

Methods

A randomized controlled trial was conducted among CKD patients aged over 65 years. The participants were randomly assigned to receive either oral mixed BCAA supplementation (60% leucine, 4.5 g/day; 20% valine, 1.5 g/day; 20% isoleucine, 1.5 g/day) (N = 29) or a placebo (N = 26) for 12 weeks. Muscle mass, serum insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), and myostatin levels were measured at baseline and after 12 weeks. A 3-day food record was reviewed by a dietitian, and functional capacity was assessed using handgrip and 6-min walk tests.

Results

Fifty-five patients (mean age 75.4 ± 5.2 years) were enrolled. Daily protein and calorie intake were comparable between groups. At study conclusion, lean muscle mass significantly increased in the leucine group compared to placebo (0.4 kg [95% CI 0.1-0.7] vs. - 0.2 kg [95% CI - 0.6-0.2], P = 0.010). A significant difference in the percentage change in muscle mass was also observed (1.0 ± 1.8% vs. - 0.5 ± 2.6%, P = 0.014). No significant differences were found in muscle strength, serum myostatin, IGF-1, or adverse events.

Conclusions

Leucine-enriched BCAA supplementation for 12 weeks significantly increased muscle mass but did not impact biomarkers of muscle activity or functional capacity in elderly CKD patients.

Clinical trial registration

TCTR20200314003.

frozen_eligibility_criteria.name: Human administered-preparation functional contrast with concurrent control
frozen_eligibility_criteria.eligibility: Human results report with an actually administered compound, biologic, extract, mixture or defined food/drink preparation; a measured functional endpoint and an identifiable concurrent randomized or nonrandomized comparator. Crossover and factorial designs are retained with their actual contrast.
frozen_eligibility_criteria.limits: No minimum effect, significance, BUB1B connection, catalog match or full-text availability requirement. Nutrient/energy mismatch does not remove eligibility; it limits ingredient attribution.

frozen_eligibility_criteria.name: Human administered-preparation function without a concurrent control
frozen_eligibility_criteria.eligibility: Actual administration and measured function, but only before/after, single-arm, case-series, historical-control or other uncontrolled evidence.
frozen_eligibility_criteria.limits: Preserve as a separate design stratum; never label a within-arm change a randomized treatment effect.

frozen_eligibility_criteria.name: Human administered-preparation nonfunctional or mechanism-only evidence
frozen_eligibility_criteria.eligibility: Actual administration with only mass, composition, molecular, metabolic, exposure, safety or other nonfunctional endpoints established by available information.
frozen_eligibility_criteria.limits: Do not infer absence of functional outcomes from an uninformative abstract; use U when scope is unclear. Relevant linked harms remain part of the functional study-family review.

frozen_eligibility_criteria.name: Preclinical administered-preparation functional experiment
frozen_eligibility_criteria.eligibility: Actual compound/preparation administration in nonhuman organisms or isolated tissue with measured task performance, locomotor output, force, power, endurance or other prespecified physiological function.
frozen_eligibility_criteria.limits: Separate organismal from ex-vivo/tissue function, species, disease model and assay; do not transfer a biomarker, viability or cellular readout to human muscle function.

frozen_eligibility_criteria.name: Preclinical administered-preparation mechanistic experiment
frozen_eligibility_criteria.eligibility: Actual compound/preparation exposure with cellular/molecular, chromosome-fidelity, metabolism, mass, viability or other mechanistic endpoints, without an established organismal/tissue functional contrast in the available record.
frozen_eligibility_criteria.limits: Preserve target/assay/dose context and all reported directions. A gene-only manipulation is a separate context record, not evidence of actual-compound administration.

frozen_eligibility_criteria.name: Context/document roles, retained separately
frozen_eligibility_criteria.eligibility: Assign a role only from explicit recorded evidence, with reason and evidence locator. A registry or conference record reporting original results is not automatically protocol-only. A review is a navigation/synthesis source, not a new randomized cohort.
frozen_eligibility_criteria.limits: Not eligible for a direct administered-compound functional contrast does not mean scientifically negative or irrelevant. Linked protocols/notices/reviews remain available to study-family review.

frozen_eligibility_criteria.name: Uncertain eligibility
frozen_eligibility_criteria.eligibility: Insufficient available information or unresolved conflicting metadata. Retain candidate routes and the exact missing fact.
frozen_eligibility_criteria.limits: No abstract, no keyword, inaccessible full text or an absent BUB1B mention is never a negative-science or ineligible label.
